description: Everyday problems around landlords, leases and deposits, living with roommates, hunting for an apartment, moving house, and buying a home.

items.title: Splitting shared bills unevenly
items.problem: Utilities, internet and streaming arrive on different days in one person's name; that person fronts the money and then has to chase everyone else for their share.
items.workaround: Venmo requests and a group chat; Splitwise for some households

items.title: Shared groceries nobody tracks
items.problem: Milk, toilet paper and dish soap get bought by whoever notices first, so the same person always pays and resentment builds.
items.workaround: Mental tally or 'you get it next time'

items.title: Rent shares for unequal rooms
items.problem: Roommates argue over how much each should pay when bedrooms differ in size, closets, windows or private bathrooms.

items.title: Collecting rent before the due date
items.problem: One roommate is on the lease and must gather everyone's portion by the first; late transfers put their own credit and deposit at risk.

items.title: Departing roommate's final settle-up
items.problem: When someone moves out mid-lease, nobody can reconstruct who owes what for the deposit, last utilities and shared furniture.
items.workaround: Argument over text; someone eats the loss

items.title: Shared furniture ownership at split
items.problem: Couches and TVs bought jointly become disputes when the household breaks up because nobody recorded who paid.

items.title: Chores rotation that nobody follows
items.problem: Dishes and trash rotations agreed verbally are forgotten within weeks and one person silently ends up doing everything.
items.workaround: Paper chart on the fridge; passive-aggressive notes

items.title: Guests staying over without warning
items.problem: A roommate's partner effectively moves in, using utilities and space, with no agreed limit or way to raise it without conflict.

items.title: Quiet hours and noise disputes
items.problem: Roommates with different schedules clash over late-night noise and early alarms and have no neutral record of agreed rules.
items.workaround: House rules discussed once, then forgotten

items.title: Shared bathroom and kitchen scheduling
items.problem: Morning bathroom time and kitchen use collide when several people leave for work at the same hour.

items.title: Missing packages in shared entryway
items.problem: Deliveries left in a common hall or lobby vanish or get taken inside by a roommate who forgets to mention it.
items.workaround: Ask in group chat; ship to work

items.title: Vetting a stranger as roommate
items.problem: Finding a replacement roommate means judging strangers from a few messages, with no easy way to check references, habits or reliability.

items.title: Roommate agreement never written down
items.problem: House rules on cleaning, guests, pets and moving out are agreed verbally and then disputed months later.

items.title: Maintenance requests going unanswered
items.problem: A broken heater or leaking tap is reported by text and then nothing happens; the tenant has no record and no way to escalate.

items.title: No paper trail with landlord
items.problem: Conversations happen by phone or in passing, so when a dispute arises the tenant cannot prove what was promised or when.

items.title: Rent receipts and payment proof
items.problem: Cash or bank-transfer rent leaves no receipt, so tenants cannot prove payment history for disputes or future applications.

items.title: Knowing tenant rights locally
items.problem: Tenants do not know what notice periods, deposit limits or repair obligations apply in their city, and rules differ by jurisdiction.

items.title: Landlord entering without notice
items.problem: Landlords or contractors show up unannounced and tenants lack a simple log of entries to support a complaint.

items.title: Rent increase arrives with no context
items.problem: A renewal offer with a big increase gives the tenant no way to check comparable rents or legal caps before responding.

items.title: Automating rent payment reliably
items.problem: Landlords accept only checks or one specific app, so tenants juggle transfers and fear a missed or late payment fee.

items.title: Move-in condition never documented
items.problem: Tenants forget to photograph scuffs and stains at move-in and later lose deposit money for pre-existing damage.
items.workaround: Phone photos scattered in camera roll

items.title: Lease renewal deadline sneaks up
items.problem: Notice-to-vacate or renewal windows pass unnoticed, locking tenants into another year or a month-to-month premium.

items.title: Understanding dense lease clauses
items.problem: Leases are long PDFs full of fees, auto-renewals and penalties that tenants sign without understanding.

items.title: Getting the deposit back on time
items.problem: After moving out, tenants wait weeks past the legal deadline with no itemized deductions and no idea how to push back.

items.title: Tracking recurring fees beyond rent
items.problem: Pet rent, parking, trash, amenity and 'admin' fees vary monthly and tenants cannot tell if they are being overcharged.

items.title: Subletting or breaking a lease
items.problem: Tenants who must leave early cannot easily find a qualified sublettor or figure out the exact penalty and process.

items.title: Renters insurance lapses unnoticed
items.problem: A required renters policy auto-renews or lapses silently, and tenants cannot find the certificate when the landlord asks.

items.title: Scam and duplicate listings
items.problem: Apartment searches are polluted by fake listings, bait-and-switch prices and the same unit posted five times.
items.workaround: Reverse image search; avoiding deals that look too good

items.title: Listings gone by the time you call
items.problem: Units marked available are already rented, wasting hours of calls and tours on stale inventory.
items.workaround: Message dozens of listings at once

items.title: Comparing units across many sites
items.problem: Candidates live across several sites, texts and emails, making it hard to compare price, commute and features side by side.

items.title: True monthly cost is hidden
items.problem: Listed rent excludes utilities, parking, fees and broker commission, so real cost is unknown until the application stage.

items.title: Commute and neighborhood unknowns
items.problem: It is hard to judge commute time at rush hour, noise, safety and grocery access for an unfamiliar address before touring.

items.title: Repeating the same application info
items.problem: Every application asks for the same pay stubs, references and IDs, and each charges a fee with no shared file.
items.workaround: Folder of PDFs re-uploaded each time

items.title: Forgetting details after tours
items.problem: After viewing several units in a day, memories blur and tenants cannot recall which one had the broken window or good light.

items.title: Tour scheduling back-and-forth
items.problem: Arranging viewings means trading texts with multiple agents around work hours, often with no-shows.

items.title: Rental application rejection blackout
items.problem: Applicants hear nothing after applying and do not know whether to keep searching or wait.

items.title: Coordinating the moving timeline
items.problem: Utilities cutover, movers, elevator booking, key handoff and cleaning all must line up on one day and one is always missed.

items.title: Not knowing what is in which box
items.problem: After a move, needed items are buried in unlabeled or vaguely labeled boxes for weeks.

items.title: Changing address everywhere
items.problem: Banks, employer, subscriptions, DMV, insurers and delivery apps each need an address update and some are forgotten for months.

items.title: Getting honest moving quotes
items.problem: Mover quotes vary wildly, hide fees, and reviews are hard to trust, so people overpay or get held hostage on delivery.

items.title: Overlapping rent during a move
items.problem: Lease dates rarely line up, forcing double rent or a scramble for storage and a place to stay in between.

items.title: Utility setup and shutoff timing
items.problem: Electricity, gas and internet must be stopped at the old place and started at the new one, and gaps or overlaps cost money.

items.title: Deciding what to sell or toss
items.problem: Before a move, deciding what to keep, sell, donate or discard is overwhelming and left to the last night.

items.title: Finding friends with a truck
items.problem: Rounding up helpers and a vehicle for a DIY move means chasing favors and last-minute cancellations.

items.title: Tracking homes viewed and rejected
items.problem: House hunters see dozens of listings and cannot remember which they toured, what they disliked or what it later sold for.

items.title: Estimating real monthly ownership cost
items.problem: Buyers see the list price but struggle to add taxes, insurance, HOA dues, PMI and maintenance into a true monthly figure.
items.workaround: Mortgage calculators that omit most costs

items.title: Closing paperwork and deadlines
items.problem: Inspection contingencies, appraisal, insurance binder and lender document requests arrive in a rush with hard deadlines.

items.title: Rent versus buy uncertainty
items.problem: Renters cannot tell whether buying makes sense for their city, savings and time horizon without a spreadsheet they distrust.

items.title: Inspection report is hard to prioritize
items.problem: A 60-page inspection lists everything from cosmetic to structural and buyers cannot tell what to negotiate or budget for.
